title: Docker Compose
idea: Docker Compose lets you describe a multi-container app in one `compose.yaml` file, then start all of it with one command.
points: Each `services` entry describes one part of your app, such as `api` or `db`.
`docker compose up` builds or pulls images, creates a network, then starts the containers.
Compose keys mirror `docker run` flags: `ports` is `-p`, `environment` is `-e`.
`${DB_PASSWORD}` is filled from your shell or from a `.env` file beside `compose.yaml`.

steps.caption: `docker compose up` reads `compose.yaml` from the current folder. It names two services: `api` and `db`.
A service with `build` is built; a service with `image` is pulled if it is missing.
Compose creates one private network for the whole project. Every container joins it.
Containers start in `depends_on` order: `db` first, then `api`. The app is running.
`docker compose down` works backwards. It stops and removes the containers.
Then it removes the network. The images stay on disk.

code.title: compose.yaml
code.caption: Two services, `api` and `db`. Save the file next to the Dockerfile.

walk.text: `api` is built from the Dockerfile in this folder, like `docker build .`.
Like `-p 3000:3000`. Keep the quotes: YAML can misread an unquoted `HOST:CONTAINER`.
`db` runs a ready-made image, pulled from Docker Hub if it is missing.
The `postgres` image requires a password; `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` sets it.

code.title: Run it
code.caption: `demo-password` is a demo value. Keep your real `.env` out of git.

walk.text: Create the `.env` file Compose reads for `${DB_PASSWORD}`.
Build `api`, create the network and start both containers in the background.
Stop and remove the containers and the network.

pitfalls: `depends_on` waits for start, not readiness; add a `healthcheck` with `condition: service_healthy`.
After code changes run `docker compose up --build`; plain `up` can reuse the old image.
Old guides use `docker-compose` and `version:`; current Compose uses `docker compose` and no `version`.

quiz.q: You run `docker compose up -d`, then `docker compose down`. What still exists?
quiz.why: `down` removes the containers and the network. Images stay on disk unless you add `--rmi`.

takeaway: Describe the app once in `compose.yaml`, then run it all with `docker compose up`.

starters: What is the difference between `docker compose` and `docker-compose`?
